newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 97/98 budget may be formed without delay - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan 97/98 budget may be formed without delay - MOF.

text.p: The Japanese government would be able to form a state budget for 1997/98 on schedule if the new government delayed the introduction of an extra budget until January, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said on Monday.

"If the (new) government decides to go ahead (with the said schedule for the extra budget), it will be possible to form the state budget (for the fiscal year starting April 1) within this year, which is important for the economy," Ogawa said.

Japan usually makes a draft state budget for the next fiscal year by the end of December, and this is debated in the regular session of parliament from January. Leaving the introduction of the extra budget until January would enable the government to concentrate its efforts on the 1997/98 budget now.

A senior official with Japan's Liberal Democratic Party, Taku Yamazaki, was quoted as saying by media reports last week that Japan will discuss the issue of the supplementary budget at the start of the regular parliament session.

Japan needs to come up with an extra budget this fiscal year to finance spending on reconstruction of areas hit by the Kobe earthquake. But it has yet to decide on whether to include economic stimulative steps in a supplementary budget.
Ogawa also reiterated the economy was currently heading for a steady recovery and that a decision on stimulative steps would be made after looking at economic conditions.
